hardware.candidate_role: USB/display signer ASCII punctuation review-renderer smoke
hardware.tested_state: host-core review renderer keeps supported printable ASCII punctuation readable while firmware keeps signing disabled

procedure: Added host-core regression coverage proving supported printable ASCII punctuation is not expanded into U+XXXX fallback text.
Added host-buildable raster coverage for a concrete punctuation glyph used by the ESP-IDF display path.
Ran NostrSeal/esp32 make ci before flashing.
Exported ESP-IDF v5.5.4 from /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/export.sh in the same shell invocation used for build, flash, and smoke.
Verified idf.py and esptool.py paths and confirmed idf.py --version reported ESP-IDF v5.5.4.
Built clean app version 571cc48 with make idf-build.
Flashed bootloader, app, and partition table to /dev/cu.usbmodem1101 and verified image hashes.
expected_result: The firmware image containing the ASCII punctuation renderer change still preserves the disabled-signing USB protocol contract.
observed_result: ESP-IDF v5.5.4 built app version 571cc48 with binary size 0x8e660 and 0x719a0 bytes free in the app partition. esptool detected ESP32-S3 QFN56 revision v0.2 with native USB-Serial/JTAG and MAC ec:da:3b:95:32:98, wrote bootloader, app, and partition-table images, and verified hashes. The smoke passed with 35 verified exchanges: 8 valid response frames and 27 expected rejection frames. get_signing_status kept signing_enabled false and sign_event remained signing_disabled.
limitations: Protocol smoke only; it does not visually verify every punctuation glyph on the physical display.
The T-Display S3 bitmap-font path still represents unsupported non-ASCII content as explicit U+XXXX fallback text.
No production key custody, secure boot, flash encryption, debug-lock, companion signed-output verification, or real signing acceptance was tested.
sign_event is expected to remain signing_disabled until trusted display review, physical approval, provisioning, storage, signed-output verification, and firmware hardening gates are complete.
